name: George Santayana
biography: Presented as James's temperamental opposite: a 'Catholic free-thinker' who appreciated religion aesthetically and historically without belief in its dogmas, an attitude James (whose doctor's thesis Santayana had called 'the perfection of rottenness') regarded as immoral. Quoted criticizing Dewey for a 'pervasive quasi-Hegelian tendency to dissolve the individual into his social functions,' corroborating Russell's own reading of Dewey.
